summary: Surge in p99 and 504s after traffic routed to cross-region sparse variant during autoscaler event
description:
Issue summary: Acme Analytics reported a spike in request p99 latency and a surge of 504s starting 2026-03-12 12:10 UTC. Root cause suspected: routing policy sent a fraction of steady-state traffic from their us-west deployment to an eu-west sparse/quantized variant that was initializing, causing KV cache coldness and long model warmups.

Impact: Approximately 12% of requests experienced >5s p99; customer reported user-facing timeouts and increased error rates on production ingestion endpoints. No data loss, but severe degradation of SLAs for the affected routes.

Environment: Dedicated capacity for Acme Analytics in prod (us-west primary). Canary and fallback policies allowed cross-region failover to eu-west when local autoscaler briefly marked several us-west replicas as constrained.

Observed behavior: Routing decision machine selected the sparse-quantized eu-west variant because it satisfied the cost/latency policy at policy-eval time, but the target replicas were still initializing and had disabled KV caching. Requests sent there were subject to cold KV misses and model cold-starts leading to serialization of warmup and high tail latency (and some 504s when request deadlines exceeded).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In a dedicated prod deployment with traffic pinned to us-west, induce an autoscaler event that marks 2/6 local replicas as constrained (simulate heavy compute).
2) Ensure routing policy allows cross-region fallback for 'cost-savings' threshold.
3) Trigger steady request stream at typical customer QPS for ~10 minutes.
4) Observe routing logs; a percentage of requests will be diverted to eu-west sparse variant which is in 'initializing' state.
5) Measure p50/p95/p99 and 504 count on affected route.

comments: [2026-03-12 12:25] Support (Leah Park): Triage: customer reports intermittent timeouts; opened internal escalation to SRE. Notified customer that we are investigating and suggested a temporary pin to their primary variant.

[2026-03-12 12:40] SRE (Mateo Ruiz): Observed routing decisions sending ~13% of traffic to eu-west sparse-quantized variant which is in initializing state. Investigating autoscaler decision that flagged local replicas as constrained.

[2026-03-12 13:05] Engineering (Sofia Chen): Confirmed kv_cache disabled on new eu-west replicas due to a config drift in image v2.3.4; replicas warmup serialized. Proposed immediate mitigation: disable cross-region fallback for this customer and pre-warm eu-west replicas if we plan to route there.
[2026-03-12 13:30] Support (Leah Park): Applied temporary pinning on customer's routing policy to force local-us-west variants. Customer reports latency return to normal; errors reduced to baseline.
[2026-03-13 09:10] Engineering (Mateo Ruiz): Deployed routing gate fix that prevents routing to initializing replicas; also hot-fixed config drift in eu-west image to enable KV caching by default.
[2026-03-14 11:45] Support (Leah Park): Followed up with customer to confirm post-fix behavior. Customer accepted resolution and requested notes on preventing recurrence.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler scaled down local capacity or marked replicas constrained, triggering cross-region fallback policy.
Telemetry shows routing evaluation picked eu-west sparse variant due to transient score improvement (cost + nominal latency) but did not account for replica readiness state in final decision.
Replica logs show 'kv_cache=disabled' and model warmup RPCs queued; cold KV misses observed on first token requests, causing long tail latency.
Observed config drift: image tag v2.3.4 built on 2026-03-05 had an opt-in flag for KV cache not set; recent eu-west rollout used that image and left replicas without prefix caching.
Related to known fallback risk (see SUP-33421) but this occurrence included cross-region network penalty plus cold start, making impact larger.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigations applied: 1) Temporarily disabled cross-region fallback for Acme Analytics routing policy; 2) Pinned traffic to us-west variants for safe period; 3) Contacted customer and advised to validate during scheduled traffic window.

Engineering fixes rolled out: 1) Hotfix to image v2.3.4 to enable KV cache by default and restart eu-west replicas; 2) Routing change to respect replica readiness (state != initializing) as a hard precondition for variant selection; 3) Add gating metric in policy eval to penalize variants with 'kv_cache=disabled' until warmup completes.

Result: After mitigation p99 decreased to baseline within 20 minutes and 504s dropped to zero for the pinned routes. No further cross-region diversions observed for the customer after gating introduced.
follow_up_tasks: Update rollout checklist to include KV cache flag verification for all quantized images (owner: Sofia Chen, due: 2026-03-20)
Add a prewarm/auto-warm policy for cross-region variant activation (owner: Mateo Ruiz, due: 2026-04-01)
Create monitoring alert that fires when routing decisions send >5% traffic to replicas in 'initializing' state (owner: Infra Observability, due: 2026-03-22)
Review routing policy scoring to include explicit readiness penalties and network region penalty (owner: Routing Team, due: 2026-03-28)
